answer: A storage market rejects an earning identity unless it proves custody of a distinct 1 TB shard set in synchronized checks, so each extra alias needs another 1 TB. The haven registry assigns random incompressible data, maps its atlas, and probes each identity vertex at once. A disk cannot reuse the same bytes for distinct assignments. This assumes unpredictable checks and deadlines shorter than fetching missing shards; a large storage owner can still buy many identities.
